flashcards.q: What are the three components of an Azure RBAC role assignment?
flashcards.a: Security principal, role definition, and scope. This decouples permissions (role definition) from resources (scope) unlike AWS, which bundles actions and resource ARNs into a single policy document.

flashcards.q: How does Azure RBAC scope inheritance work?
flashcards.a: Scope forms a strict hierarchy: management group -> subscription -> resource group -> resource. A role assigned at a higher scope is automatically inherited by everything beneath it -- there is no direct AWS equivalent to this cascading grant.

flashcards.q: What can Contributor NOT do that Owner can?
flashcards.a: Contributor cannot manage role assignments (no Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write) -- it structurally cannot grant access to others, even though it has full resource management rights. User Access Administrator or Owner is needed for that.

flashcards.q: What is the key difference between Azure RBAC and Azure Policy?
flashcards.a: RBAC controls who can act (identity permissions). Azure Policy controls what resource configurations are allowed to exist, regardless of who made the change. Azure has no clean equivalent to an AWS SCP permission ceiling -- the closest is rarely-hand-authored deny assignments plus Policy's deny effect on configuration state.

flashcards.q: Differentiate system-assigned vs user-assigned managed identity lifecycle.
flashcards.a: System-assigned: created 1:1 with a resource, automatically deleted when that resource is deleted. User-assigned: an independent Azure resource with its own lifecycle, attachable to many resources (up to 1000), surviving resource recreation.

flashcards.q: State the managed identity attachment and creation-rate limits.
flashcards.a: A user-assigned identity can attach to up to 1,000 resources; a single resource can have up to 20 user-assigned identities. Creation is rate-limited to 400 ops/20s per tenant/region and 80 ops/20s per subscription/region.

flashcards.q: How does a workload get a managed identity token, mechanically?
flashcards.a: It calls the local Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) at http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token with a required 'Metadata: true' header (anti-SSRF hardening), receiving a short-lived Entra ID access token scoped to the requested resource audience.

flashcards.q: What licensing tier does baseline Conditional Access require, and what requires P2?
flashcards.a: Baseline Conditional Access requires Entra ID P1. Risk-based Conditional Access (sign-in/user risk), PIM, and Identity Protection require P2. A free-tier tenant has zero Conditional Access.

flashcards.q: What is Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) and what problem does it solve?
flashcards.a: CAE revokes a token within minutes of a critical security signal (account disabled, password changed, high risk detected) instead of waiting for natural token expiry (60-90 minutes), closing the exposure window for stolen/leaked tokens. It requires the resource provider to explicitly support CAE.

flashcards.q: What does PIM do and what is 'eligible' vs 'active'?
flashcards.a: Privileged Identity Management (P2-gated) converts standing admin role assignments into eligible-only; a user activates the role on demand (MFA, justification, optional approval) for a bounded duration, after which it reverts to eligible. This is Azure's analog to AWS AssumeRole for human admins.

flashcards.q: What is the hard role-assignment limit per Azure subscription, and what doesn't count against it?
flashcards.a: 4,000 role assignments per subscription, a fixed ceiling that cannot be raised. Eligible (PIM, not yet activated) and future-scheduled assignments do not count toward this limit. Assigning to a group instead of individuals also reduces the count (one assignment covers all members).

flashcards.q: What is the custom role definition limit in Azure, and at what scope is it tracked?
flashcards.a: 5,000 custom role definitions per tenant (2,000 for the 21Vianet/China cloud), tracked tenant-wide -- roles created at the management-group scope still count against this same total.

flashcards.q: What was the 2023 Entra ID rebrand actually about?
flashcards.a: Microsoft renamed Azure Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID in 2023 -- not cosmetic, it signaled the product becoming part of a broader identity portfolio (Entra Permissions Management, Verified ID, Workload ID) rather than just the directory behind Azure.

flashcards.q: What is Entra Workload ID Federation and what AWS pattern does it mirror?
flashcards.a: OIDC-based federation letting external systems like GitHub Actions exchange a signed OIDC token for Azure access without a stored secret. It mirrors AWS's GitHub OIDC + AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity pattern -- zero long-lived credentials for CI/CD.

flashcards.q: Name a real-world limit-related failure mode with managed identity creation in automation.
flashcards.a: A Terraform apply creating many user-assigned identities in a tight loop within one subscription/region can hit the 80-creates-per-20-seconds throttle before the tenant-wide 400/20s limit, producing retriable throttling errors that look like generic API failures unless the specific limit is known.
